claims.hypothesis: Is the nuclear mid-IR emission of nearby Seyferts dominated by unresolved emission while the ALMA 870 um emission is resolved?
claims.experiment: PSF-subtraction of ground-based mid-IR images and comparison with GB21 ALMA 870 um continuum sizes
claims.result: Unresolved emission is more than 60% of the nuclear 1.5 arcsec (~150 pc) mid-IR emission in most galaxies; ALMA continuum mostly resolved
claims.finding: Mid-IR is dominated by an unresolved component at 0.3 arcsec resolution whereas the far-IR is extended

evidence.quote: The mid-IR unresolved emission contributes more than 60% of the nuclear
By contrast, the ALMA $870\,\mu$m continuum emission is mostly resolved with a median diameter of 42 pc

claims.hypothesis: Does extended mid-IR emission trace polar dust, perpendicular to the ALMA-identified torus?
claims.experiment: Overlay PSF-subtracted mid-IR contours on ALMA 870 um maps and compare with ionization cone PAs
claims.result: Six galaxies show extended mid-IR emission near the polar direction and perpendicular to the ALMA 870 um emission; NGC 6300 is equatorial
claims.finding: Polar mid-IR dust emission is common in the sample, though it may be wind or NLR edge dust and cannot be distinguished

evidence.quote: In six galaxies there is extended mid-IR emission approximately in the polar direction and perpendicular to the extended $870\,\mu$m component detected with ALMA.
With the existing data, we cannot distinguish between the two possibilities.

claims.hypothesis: Are Eddington ratios and nuclear column densities of the sample favourable to launching dusty winds?
claims.experiment: Place ALMA N_H and lambda_Edd in the diagram of Fabian2008 and Venanzi2020 predictions
claims.result: Half the sample lies in the region favourable to polar and/or equatorial dusty winds; some have too high N_H or low lambda_Edd
claims.finding: Polar mid-IR emission is found preferentially at moderate N_H and Eddington ratios and higher AGN luminosity, consistent with IR radiation pressure driven winds

evidence.quote: The Eddington ratios and nuclear hydrogen column densities ($N_{\rm H}$) of half the sample are favorable to launching polar and/or equatorial dusty winds, according to numerical simulations.

claims.hypothesis: Can CAT3D-WIND disk+wind models explain the observed unresolved fractions and mid/far-IR morphologies?
claims.experiment: Generate 1728 + 9 model images, convolve to 0.3 and 0.1 arcsec, apply PSF subtraction, compare qualitatively
claims.result: Models reproduce qualitative aspects; low to intermediate wind-to-disk ratio (up to ~0.6) is required to match large unresolved mid-IR fractions
claims.finding: Observations support the torus+wind scenario, with the wind component more relevant at high Eddington ratio or luminosity

evidence.quote: However, low to intermediate values of the wind-to-disk ratio are required to account for the observed large fractions of unresolved mid-IR emission in our sample.
This work and Paper I provide observational support for the torus+wind scenario.

why_this_data.value: GB21 ALMA observations of a volume-limited, complete sample of Seyferts drawn from the Swift-BAT survey

evidence.quote: obtained ALMA observations of a volume-limited and complete sample of Seyfert galaxies to study their torus properties

why_this_method.value: Model images explore mid- and far-IR morphologies for several disk and wind configurations informed by IR fits

evidence.loc: 5 CAT3D-WIND mid- and far-IR model images
evidence.quote: The goal is to explore the morphologies at these wavelengths for several disk and wind configurations and geometries as informed by fits to their IR emission.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Polar mid-IR emission could be AGN-driven dusty outflow and/or dust at NLR/cone edges; torus models without a wind can also give one-sided morphologies via self-obscuration

evidence.quote: The extended mid-IR emission along the polar direction is likely associated with AGN-driven dusty outflows (cite: Wada2018; Williamson2020; Venanzi2020) and/or dust located in the edges of the NLR and ionization cones.
Torus models without the wind component can also produce this one-sided polar emission at intermediate inclinations and relatively large torus angular widths

limitations_admitted.value: PSF stability of ground-based mid-IR data limits extraction of extended emission

evidence.quote: One of the main caveats from the analysis of the extended mid-IR emission with ground-based facilities is the stability of the PSF.

limitations_admitted.value: Emission lines in imaging filters may contribute to polar alignment in some galaxies

evidence.quote: might be partly responsible for the alignment along the polar direction

limitations_admitted.value: Model comparison depends on assumed sublimation radius; case-by-case comparison needs better r_sub and resolution

evidence.quote: Detailed morphological comparisons on a case-by-case basis require accurate estimates of the sublimation radius as well as higher angular resolution observations, especially in the mid-IR.
